SmartPixels Tier-2¶

From inner-pixel hits to Level-1 trigger capability¶

digiRefit → refit-quality BDT → coherent downstream reco → jet tagging & vertexing

Nick Manganelli — SmartPixels internal talk — July 2026

Interactive deck: the refit-replay visualizer and the MVA explorer are live HTML — links on their slides.

[0:00 – 0:30] Welcome. This is an internal status talk: everything shown exists and runs today. Audience calibration: we have CMS/ATLAS experts, Muon Collider students, undergrads, and ASIC engineers in the room — everyone knows pixel detectors; not everyone knows CMS L1 jargon, so I'll define terms as they appear. 30 minutes of content, dark-sector physics in backup.

The thesis¶

Better inner-pixel information → better L1 tracks → new trigger capability.

CMS Phase-2 L1 tracks are built from the outer tracker only (r > 25 cm). SmartPixels asks: what if the trigger could also see the inner pixel barrel (r < 16 cm), where impact parameters and vertices actually live?

The R&D-payoff framing — each layer of this work stands on its own:

layer Phase-2-baseline value even if SmartPixels is never adopted
track refit machinery pixel-augmented L1 tracking studies, truth-linked nano tooling
refit-quality BDT track-quality MVA methodology, bit-exact FPGA (conifer) path
tagger / vertex R&D L1 jet-flavor + vertexing improvements on the baseline track trigger

[0:30 – 1:30] One minute. The thesis sentence is the whole talk. For non-CMS people: the Level-1 trigger is the 40 MHz hardware decision layer; Phase-2 CMS puts tracking in it for the first time, but only from the outer tracker. The payoff table is the de-risking argument: this R&D produces upstreamable spinoffs regardless of whether SmartPixels itself is adopted — say this explicitly, it frames every result that follows.

Cheat sheet (CMS-isms used in this talk)¶

term meaning
L1 / L1T Level-1 trigger: 40 MHz custom-hardware decision layer (FPGA, µs latency)
OT / IT outer tracker (r ≈ 25–110 cm) / inner tracker = pixels (TBPX barrel, r ≈ 3–16 cm)
L1TT / TTTrack Phase-2 L1 Track Trigger; its track object (rinv, φ0, tanλ, z0, d0)
stub correlated hit pair in an OT pT-module — the L1 tracking primitive
TP TrackingParticle: the truth particle a reco track is matched to
GTT Global Track Trigger: track-only trigger objects (primary vertex, sums)
PF / PUPPI Particle Flow (link tracks+calo into candidates) / per-particle pileup weighting
SC4 / SC8 seeded-cone L1 jets, R = 0.4 / 0.8
KF Kalman filter: sequential fit update, one measurement at a time

Skippable cheat sheet — keep it up for 15 seconds, tell people to photograph it. For the undergrads: the one concept to hold is that a stub is the outer-tracker primitive and a TTTrack is a 5-parameter helix fit through stubs, with the two impact parameters d0 (transverse) and z0 (longitudinal) describing where the track passes closest to the beamline.

Where Tier-2 came from: the tier model¶

Separate what exists from what is being rehearsed:

tier status what it is
Tier 3 — refit reserved the true system: consumes a real SmartTracklet collection from a future L1 SmartPixels track finder (mode name + config plumbed, raises if selected)
Tier 2 — digiRefit implemented OT L1Tracks projected into TBPX; hit candidates are the real persisted pixel digis — occupancy, combinatorics and fakes come for free; only the cluster angle information is synthesized
Tier 1 — TP-projection toys footnote degenerate path of the same producer

Tier-2 truth is per-digi via PixelDigiSimLink: a same-TP digi gets angles from the track's own parent, an other-TP digi from its parent, a no-link digi from a noise distribution — correct fake phenomenology by construction.

[1:30 – 3:30] Two minutes, one slide. The point for experts: Tier 2 is not a toy — the digis are the real ones from the simulation chain, so window occupancy and combinatoric fakes are honest; the only synthesized ingredient is the cluster-shape angle info a SmartPixels ASIC would provide (that is what the ASIC engineers in the room would eventually supply for real). One truth-posture line if asked: production runs "posture C" — tracks rebuilt in-job from the file's persisted stubs, giving real pileup and genuine seed covariance. Details in backup.

NanoAOD capability, today¶

One flat, columnar file per configuration carries the whole loop (production → training → eval):

  • Extended SmartPix nano flavors — tracks + PF + jets + gen in one file (L1PFTrkNanoSmartPix+withGen)
  • Per-variant track tables — refit output for each layer config, row-aligned with the reference L1TTrack
  • Refit sidecar — per-hit link tables: χ² increments, pulls, window multiplicity, hit-truth class
  • Truth by index — matched-TP full parameters on every track (tp_d0, tp_z0, tp_phi, production vertex) → resolution-vs-truth offline, no re-matching
  • Jet side — SC4 and SC8 seeded-cone jets, PF-candidate link tables (−1/−2 sentinel convention), embedded OT stubs

[3:30 – 6:30] Three minutes over two slides. Skip the history entirely — this is "what we CAN do now". For the tree-level-analysis crowd: this is NanoAOD, so everything downstream is uproot/awkward, no framework needed. The key design idea to voice: row alignment — variant tables are index-aligned to the reference track table, so truth and features cross-reference by index, never by geometric re-matching.

Two coherent nano products (both proven in production)¶

Fat coherent nano — one config, fully coherent downstream: refit tracks → re-run Layer-1 correlator + vertex in-job → PF → PUPPI → SC4/SC8 jets all computed from the refit tracks (nano_fat_{1111,1100}_coopt, 0000_baseline).

  • Proven non-trivial: naive downstream injection was byte-identical to the file's products; the in-job correlator re-run is what makes jets/vertex/PF actually see the refit.

Multi-mode co-registered nano — all 15 refit variants per event, one coherent shard (nano_pG): every layer config side by side on the same events → config ablations from a single file.

The subtle point (worth 30 seconds for the experts): the correlator inputs are persisted products built from the original tracks, so simply relabeling collections changes nothing — we proved a naive injection produced byte-identical jets. The fix re-emulates the correlator regions + the FastHisto vertex inside the nano job, pointed at the refit tracks. That is what "coherent" means every time I say it in the tagger section.

Tier-2 digiRefit¶

the approach, what works, and what does not (yet)¶

[6:30] Section marker — announce this is the core ~11 minutes of the talk.

The idea¶

5-par OT-only seed vs 5-par OT+IT refit (promptHnpar=5, real fitted d0): project the TTTrack helix into TBPX, open a per-layer window of real pixel digis, synthesize the cluster angles (α, β), select at most one hit per layer, and apply a Kalman update to the 5-parameter track state at each layer.

Producer pipeline (per track): window collection → digi truth-classification & angle synthesis → hit selection → sequential scalar KF update (numerical Jacobian) → loud-failure guards. Same helix projector shared with the payload analyzer — single implementation, no drift.

[6:30 – 8:30] The figure is the explanation: left panel shows the lever arm (track fit way out at 25–110 cm, extrapolated inward), right panel the per-layer windows and the POCA where d0/z0 sharpen. For undergrads: a Kalman update is just "merge the prediction with one new measurement, weighted by uncertainties". For experts: 5-parameter prompt seed — we deliberately anchor on promptHnpar=5 so the seed has a real fitted d0; the b-tagging /di-Higgs use-case demands it, and the 4-par pinned-d0 path is dropped everywhere in this talk.

The centerpiece: step-by-step refit replay (interactive)¶

Open in a browser tab: ../eval_refitq/refitviz/refit_replay.html — self-contained ~17 MB HTML, no server, no kernel.

  • per-KF-step replay: slider / play / step buttons through each layer's update
  • seed (OT-only) vs refit helix, covariance bands, per-step parameter deltas
  • full-hit-set χ² column — reduced χ² including the OT stubs, seed row → per-layer rows → refit row → truth footer
  • 15 layer configs × 3 angle modes (none / α / α+β), curated real tracks (clean genuine / wrong-hit pickup / fake)

[8:30 – 12:00] THE demo — give it 3+ minutes. Have it open in a dedicated browser tab beforehand (the iframe works in the exported slides; in JupyterLab prefer the tab). Suggested script: (1) clean genuine track, AAAA, alphaBeta — step the KF layer by layer, watch d0/z0 bands tighten toward the truth row; (2) flip angle mode none→alphaBeta on the same track to show what the ASIC angle info buys; (3) the fake track — watch the full-hit-set chi2 column explode: that is a feature, it is the discrimination the quality BDT will use. For ASIC engineers: the angle mode toggle is exactly their deliverable's physics value, live.

The sign bug: what the visualizer caught¶

Act 1 — the symptom. Long-running L3/L4 inefficiency and KF instability; χ² blow-ups; a saga of clamp "band-aids". Aggregate metrics: nothing obviously wrong.

Act 2 — the visualizer. First event on screen: the projected seed helix curled to the mirror-image azimuthal side of its own hits — the helix projector's parametrization curled opposite to the TTTrack rinv sign convention. Error grows as r²/R: ≈0 at L1, ≈2 mm at L4 → pulls up to 142σ. Invisible at L1, fatal at L4.

Act 3 — triple verification, one-line fix.

  1. circle-fit through the track's own OT stubs: R = 388 cm = stored 1/|rinv| — helix lands on its stubs only with negated curvature
  2. per-layer residuals grow monotonically L1→L4 (0.23 mm → 2.3 mm); post-fix flat at ≈0.05 mm
  3. matched-TP truth helix confirms the stored curvature sign was right — the formula was wrong

Fix: const double rInv = -h.rInv; at projector entry. The clamps it was fighting are now inert.

Lesson: interactive event-level inspection catches what aggregate metrics hide.

[12:00 – 14:30] The narrative beat — tell it as a story, ~2.5 min. Emphasize the shape of the failure: a sign error whose magnitude grows quadratically with radius, so every L1-anchored sanity check passed. The triple verification matters for credibility with the experts: geometry (stubs), statistics (residual growth), truth (TP handedness) — three independent witnesses. And the punchline for everyone: months of clamp archaeology, one line of code.

Post-fix: truth-validated resolution at scale¶

184,839 matched tracks / 1000 PU events (10-file post-fix production, matched-TP truth): d0 389 → 210 µm (−46%), z0 1430 → 626 µm (−56%) for the all-layer config. The 5-par prompt seed (promptHnpar=5) is validated at production scale.

Note the fine print the medians reveal: AAII (L1+L2 only) beats AAAA on the median — outer IT layers add wrong-hit pickup (multiple scattering widens the window) alongside their constraint. Real, understood, and part of the limitations slide.

[14:30 – 16:00] The money plot for the refit. Everything here is |reco − matched-TP truth| median, not seed→refit deltas — resolution toward truth is the honest metric. For the b-tagging crowd: 210 µm median d0 at L1, from a trigger-track refit, is the quantity that feeds impact-parameter-based flavor tagging. The AAII-vs-AAAA inversion is a gift: it pre-announces the wrong-hit-pickup limitation with data, not apology.

Limitations, stated plainly¶

  • Low statistics: ~1000 events per config; every downstream number inherits this
  • Fake tracks: the refit χ² explodes on fakes — by design a feature (the full-hit-set χ² column is the discriminant), but fake-side behavior is measured on few-thousand-track samples
  • MS-driven wrong-hit pickup on outer IT layers — visible in the AAII < AAAA medians; needs smarter per-layer windows / hit arbitration
  • ASIC efficiency payloads are placeholders — the hooks exist (smarthitTrueSet reserved), but no real ASIC response model is wired in yet
  • KF angle clamps under review: default measAngleMaxAbs=12 is tighter than needed post-fix (fires on 0.12% of accepted-hit angles); relax to ~30–50. The clamp now only guards the persisted χ² feature from grazing-crossing garbage — it is resolution-neutral (clamp on/off identical to the last digit)

[16:00 – 17:30] Do not rush this slide; its honesty buys the tagger claims credibility. The clamp story in one breath: the sign bug made the clamps look load-bearing; post-fix they are inert for resolution and only keep the persisted chi2 BDT-input column clean — the coopt production already runs measAngleMaxAbs=30. If ASIC engineers ask: the efficiency-payload hook is exactly where their measured response model plugs in.

New capabilities on top of the refit¶

quality BDT → coherent tagger matrix → vertex R&D¶

[17:30] Section marker: ~7 minutes. The ladder: per-track quality score, then the event-level question — does any of this help jets.

Refit-quality BDT (“tkquality”)¶

  • 24-feature v1 spec (per-layer pulls, χ² increments, window occupancy, seed deltas, OT fit words)
  • genuine-vs-fake AUC 0.970–0.977 across ALL 15 layer configs — robust to which layers are instrumented
  • conifer ↔ xgboost bit-parity: offline float32 tree-walk matches the in-producer conifer::BDT (margin self-check exactly 0.0; producer parity 16410/16455 bit-exact, residuals = float32 snapshot threshold-edge cases)

[17:30 – 19:30] Two minutes. Orienting sentence: this is a per-track "is it real?" score, trained genuine-vs-fake on the refit sidecar features. The flat 0.970–0.977 band is the headline: instrument any subset of layers and the quality score works — a robustness statement the hardware people should hear. Bit-parity matters because conifer is the FPGA path: what we train offline is bit-for-bit what the firmware would compute.

Does it help the jet tagger?¶

Headline: refit-driven coherent downstream reco lifts the 8-flavor jet-tagger macro AUC by +0.044 (1111) / +0.027 (1100) over the OT-only baseline (0.686 → 0.730 / 0.713) — well outside the seed spread (±0.002–0.014).

Caveat, same breath: ~1300 test jets per view — only the 0.03–0.04 refit-vs-OT-only gap is robust; every within-view feature delta is at or below seed noise.

[19:30 – 21:30] The tagger headline and its caveat live on the same slide on purpose. Mechanism, one sentence: the lift is NOT from adding a feature to the tagger — it comes from the vertex→PF→PUPPI→jet chain being re-computed from the refit tracks (the fat coherent nanos), i.e., better tracks propagate through the whole event reconstruction. For skeptics: 3 seeds per cell, best-of-seed shown with spread; the 11-cell matrix is in the json.

The feature-level story is coherent too¶

  • refit-BDT score as a tagger input: small positive (+0.003, within noise) — but consistently lifts taus (τ+ AUC 0.706 → 0.733 on 1111)
  • vertex-dxy feature helps only where there is no refit: 0000 baseline 0.686 → 0.694 (+0.008); redundant on refit views — once tracks carry a real impact parameter, the vertex proxy adds nothing
  • charge head trains for free: +charge output on the full feature set, macro AUC 0.722 — no tagging cost

Each feature behaves exactly as the physics says it should — that self-consistency is the evidence the machinery is measuring something real (at these stats).

[21:30 – 22:30] One minute. This is the "physics sanity" slide: at ~1300 test jets no within-view delta is significant, but the pattern — vertex-dxy only helps the view without refit IP, the quality score helps the multiprong taus — is what you predict before looking. Say that sentence; it is the strongest low-stats statement one can honestly make.

Vertex emulators (one slide)¶

Context: baseline GTT primary vertex is FastHisto (histogram tracks in z0, pick the peak); NNVtx is the ML alternative. Our R&D on top of the refit tracks:

  • transverse vertex (dx, dy) least-squares: closed-form normal equations from track (d0, φ0) — a beam-spot-scale transverse fit from L1 tracks, with significance
  • kernel peak-finder: replace FastHisto's flat window with tapered kernels (triangular / Gaussian / Epanechnikov) — in two-close-vertices toys the tapered kernel halves the midpoint mis-pick rate
  • feeds the tagger's vertexdxy feature group (the one that lifted the OT-only view)

[24:30 – 26:00] ~1.5 minutes. Orienting sentence: the L1 primary vertex today is a 1-D histogram peak in z; we prototyped (a) the transverse companion fit that only becomes meaningful once tracks have a real d0 — i.e., only with the refit — and (b) a drop-in kernel upgrade to the histogram peak-finder itself, which is a pure Phase-2-baseline improvement (payoff framing again).

Close: the payoff, and what's next¶

Every rung already paid out: refit machinery (truth-linked nano loop) → quality BDT (bit-exact FPGA path, robust across configs) → coherent reco (+0.04 tagger AUC at low stats) — each with Phase-2-baseline value independent of SmartPixels adoption.

Next:

  1. Real production statistics — the recipe is productionized; waiting on 200-PU input procurement
  2. ASIC-fidelity payloads — wire measured ASIC response/efficiency into the reserved hooks
  3. The TS0 lever — score transmission: today the quality-BDT score reaches the tagger only offline. Making it visible to PF track selection is a config-only change (cut-strings can read trkMVA1); carrying it into the candidate word for the tagger is a hardware/word-format change — the concrete, costed ask for the hardware discussion.

[26:00 – 27:00] Close on the thesis. The TS0 lever is the actionable takeaway for the ASIC and firmware people: there is a zero-hardware step (config-only PF visibility) and a word-format step, cleanly separated. Then offer backup: dark-sector reach if there is time. Leave ~3 minutes for questions inside the 30.

Backup: dark-sector L1 sensitivity (the bonus physics)¶

  • Signature map: soft-unclustered energy patterns (SUEP flagship — rebuilt after the multiplicity-based version was refuted), displaced/low-pT track signatures needing IT-level info at L1
  • One placement, two capabilities: a proposed subsystem between {L1TrackFinder + SmartPixels track finder} and {GTT / GMT / correlator} — graph-track condensation + reseeding
  • Upstream-payoff thesis: the observables and the condensation/reseeding subsystem are contributions to the baseline Phase-2 track trigger, decoupled from SmartPixels adoption risk — speculative R&D de-risked by its spinoffs

If-time bonus (~2 min if used). Scoping + critique docs exist (DarkSectorL1Scoping.md); frame as reach, not results.

Backup: truth postures (why three)¶

Association maps are Ref-keyed — mixing collections silently breaks truth. Hence:

  • Posture B inJob (default): remake digis→stubs→tracks→maps self-consistently — all noPU development
  • Posture A fromFile: file tracks + file maps + file digis — needed when re-digitizing would lose PU; but old-layout file tracks have all-zero helix covariance → forces parametrized seeding
  • Posture C fromFileStubs (production): rebuild tracks from the file's persisted stub tier → real PU and genuine seed covariance (seedCovMode="trackCov" valid on PU files)

Backup: KF guards — post-fix status¶

guard default post-fix firing verdict
jacobianMaxAbs 10⁴ 0 inert (was a bug band-aid); can drop
chi2UpdateGate 2×10⁶ 0 keep as cheap numerical backstop
predAngleMaxAbs 12 ~5 / 100 evt cosmetic; relax freely
measAngleMaxAbs 12 0.12% of accepted-hit angles relax 12 → ~30–50, keep as guard

Clamp ON vs OFF: resolution identical to the last digit (d0 210.5 vs 210.0 µm). The clamp's only remaining job: keep the persisted χ² feature clean — with it off, the tail re-explodes to ~10⁹–10¹⁰ on ~0.1% of hits (a poisoned BDT input, not a crash). Cleaner future fix: gate the persisted χ² instead of the angle.

Backup: refit-BDT deployment path (parity receipts)¶

  • Export: train-refitquality --export-conifer → conifer JSON + metadata (feature order, spec version, margin semantics, provenance)
  • Margin semantics: conifer/producer compute the raw booster logit margin; the sklearn predict(output_margin=True) wrapper disagrees by up to 0.86 on xgboost≥2 — always reference the booster
  • Producer parity: 16410/16455 trkMVA1 bit-exact vs the float32 offline walk; the 45 residuals are float32-snapshot values crossing strict-< split thresholds (one-leaf steps)
  • Stage-3 v1 models: conifer_margin_selfcheck = 0.0 on all 15 configs
  • The score lands in trkMVA1 on the refit track word — the hook the TS0 lever builds on
